domain_assessment.domain: Elementary-school curriculum implementation and instructional program evaluation
domain_assessment.role: K-5 Curriculum Coordinator and instructional-coaching-cycle lead
domain_assessment.objective: Evaluate a six-classroom Bridge Literacy pilot, communicate a defensible interim finding to the board and finance committee, and recommend whether and how to scale the program before the budget cycle
domain_assessment.incident_type: Time-constrained checkpoint review involving data-quality verification, stakeholder communication, survey interpretation, and cautious causal attribution under implementation confounding

decision_points.summary: The coordinator decides to verify whether different benchmark-administration days distorted results across all six classrooms rather than investigate only the flat or mixed classrooms.
evidence_before: Three classrooms were above expected growth and three were flat or mixed.
The two schools administered the benchmark on different days because of a scheduling conflict.
The board needed a scale-up recommendation before the next budget cycle.
evidence_after: The specialist found testing conditions were broadly similar across all six classrooms.
One flat classroom had unusually high absenteeism, which was a more plausible explanation for that classroom's result.
goals_constraints: Determine whether a testing-window difference was a meaningful validity threat.
alternatives: Accept the gain classrooms and focus explanatory scrutiny on the flat classrooms.
Wait for a complete audit before forming any interim view.
Apply the testing-condition review consistently to all six classrooms.
decision_points.decision_basis: The scheduling issue applied generally rather than being uniquely associated with disappointing results; uniform scrutiny was needed to support a fair comparison.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate to high: the board required a recommendation before the next budget cycle and the verification occurred close to the board deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether variation in benchmark-administration dates materially affected observed growth patterns, and whether absenteeism explained one flat result.

decision_points.summary: The coordinator chooses an aggregate highlights slide for the board presentation rather than presenting all six classroom profiles individually.
evidence_before: The coordinator had the complete six-classroom data set and walkthrough-observation log.
The board agenda allowed fifteen minutes.
The math intervention team was presenting immediately afterward.
evidence_after: A board member requested classroom-level detail.
The coordinator could answer because the underlying detail was available, although it was not formatted for the presentation.
goals_constraints: Avoid exceeding the allotted agenda time.
Retain access to classroom-level evidence if challenged.
alternatives: Present all six classroom profiles individually.
Present the aggregate trend with underlying classroom data available for questions.
decision_points.decision_basis: Agenda-time limitation, paired with retention of the complete classroom-level material for follow-up.
decision_points.time_pressure: High: fifteen minutes, followed by another team presentation.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether aggregate presentation would give the board enough detail to evaluate heterogeneity across classrooms.

decision_points.summary: The coordinator interprets voluntary professional-development feedback cautiously and treats the missing response as a possible limitation rather than evidence of overall teacher sentiment.
evidence_before: Five of six pilot teachers completed the survey.
All five respondents rated the coaching session helpful or very helpful.
One respondent said the pacing guide felt rushed for lower-performing students.
The survey sample was small and voluntary.
evidence_after: The coordinator learned that the nonresponding teacher worked in a flat classroom.
The coordinator flagged the possibility of a rosier-than-full-group picture in the written summary.
goals_constraints: Avoid representing five voluntary responses as a conclusive measure of all teacher views.
Preserve uncertainty about the nonrespondent's perspective.
alternatives: Present the five positive responses as representative of teacher sentiment.
Exclude the survey entirely because of the small voluntary sample.
Report the feedback while explicitly noting voluntary-response and nonresponse limitations.
decision_points.decision_basis: The response pattern was informative but insufficiently representative to settle the broader question of teacher views.
decision_points.time_pressure: Low to moderate: the survey was summarized during the broader board-preparation process, but no immediate response from the nonresponding teacher was obtained.
decision_points.uncertainty: Whether the nonrespondent's view differed materially from the five respondents and whether the survey overstated perceived usefulness.

decision_points.summary: The coordinator recommends a staged next round and declines to attribute observed gains solely to personal coaching because coaching, materials, and class size co-occurred.
evidence_before: The aggregate pilot result was a modest net gain across six classrooms.
The coordinator made biweekly coaching visits in four classrooms.
The coached classrooms also had new decodable-text materials and, in some cases, smaller class sizes.
Two classrooms improved without direct coaching visits but had new materials, and one also had a smaller roster.
evidence_after: The memo attributes the pattern to multiple co-occurring contributors rather than coaching alone.
The coordinator recommends tracking classrooms with and without direct coaching separately in a later round.
The coordinator identifies staggering coaching versus materials-only exposure as a way to reduce causal entanglement.
goals_constraints: Make a scale-up recommendation without overstating causal certainty.
Address board questions about improvement in uncoached classrooms.
Avoid committing prematurely to a districtwide coaching build-out.
Create a more interpretable implementation design for the next round.
alternatives: Credit coaching as the primary driver of gains.
Credit materials, class size, or coaching individually without adequate separation.
Offer no scale-up recommendation until a fully disentangled design is available.
Recommend a staged implementation that preserves materials while separately tracking direct coaching exposure.
decision_points.decision_basis: The available observational pattern did not isolate coaching from materials and class size; improved uncoached classrooms directly weakened a coaching-only explanation.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate: the recommendation was needed before budget decisions, although the proposed staged approach deferred a full districtwide commitment.
decision_points.uncertainty: The independent contribution of coaching, decodable materials, class size, absenteeism, and other classroom-level differences.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: If I only went looking for problems in the rooms with disappointing numbers, I'd have no way of knowing whether the same issue was quietly present in the rooms that looked fine. It seemed like the only fair way to trust the comparison.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision point 1, participant explanation for reviewing testing conditions across all six classrooms
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No biased-assimilation mechanism is supported. The participant explicitly applies the same validity check to favorable and unfavorable outcomes, rather than selectively interpreting ambiguous evidence to preserve a preferred conclusion.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is justified methodological scrutiny: the administration-date issue was a cross-classroom measurement concern, and the coordinator appropriately assessed it across the full comparison set.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. A zero-occurrence vocabulary-control condition does not require evidence of biased assimilation; it requires the absence of a defensible instance.

revision.current_defect: None relative to the zero-target control requirement.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the uniform testing-condition review and the explicit rationale that the potential distortion applied to all classrooms, irrespective of result direction.
preserve: Uniform scrutiny across all six classrooms
The distinction between the broad testing-window concern and the classroom-specific absenteeism explanation
avoid_creating: A statement that treats favorable results as presumptively valid while treating flat results as suspect
Selective collection or weighting of evidence based on whether it supports pilot scale-up
Post hoc reinterpretation of the same ambiguous evidence to protect a prior commitment

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: I tried to lay out all of that together rather than pointing to one piece — coaching, materials, and class size were all present at the same time in the classrooms that improved most.
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Decision point 4, recommendation memo and discussion of improved classrooms without direct coaching
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: No egocentric-bias mechanism is supported. The participant declines to center the personally administered coaching activity, identifies multiple plausible contributors, and treats improvement without personal coaching as disconfirming evidence against self-credit.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant demonstrates appropriate causal humility in a confounded implementation setting. Personal involvement in coaching does not itself establish self-serving attribution.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The control requires no egocentric-bias occurrence, and the interview already contains direct evidence of distributed causal credit.

revision.location: Decision point 4, causal explanation and staged recommendation
revision.current_defect: None relative to the zero-target control requirement.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the account of co-occurring coaching, materials, and class-size factors; retain the two uncoached improving classrooms as evidence against a coaching-only narrative.
preserve: The coordinator's personal role in providing coaching
The co-occurrence of coaching, materials, and class-size variation
The plan to track classrooms with and without direct coaching separately
avoid_creating: Language crediting the coordinator's visits as the primary cause without comparative evidence
Dismissal of the uncoached improving classrooms as irrelevant or exceptional without evidentiary support
Attribution of successful outcomes to personal effort while assigning unfavorable outcomes solely to external circumstances

additional_candidate_biases.bias: Aggregation bias or masking of subgroup heterogeneity
additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: I decided to bring a highlights slide with the aggregate trend line rather than all six classrooms individually — mostly a time issue.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: An aggregate display can conceal divergent classroom-level outcomes and can sometimes cause decision-makers to overweight the overall trend relative to heterogeneous subgroup evidence.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The coordinator had a genuine fifteen-minute agenda constraint, retained classroom-level data, disclosed and answered a request for disaggregated detail, and did not claim that the aggregate result made classroom differences irrelevant. The text supports pragmatic presentation compression, not a distorted reasoning process.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: It's a small sample and it was voluntary, so I noted that caveat when I summarized it — I didn't want to present five responses as if that settled anything about how teachers overall felt.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A voluntary survey can yield systematically unrepresentative feedback if respondents differ from nonrespondents.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is a sampling limitation in the evidence source, not necessarily a cognitive bias by the participant. The coordinator explicitly recognizes the limitation and avoids treating the five responses as representative.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: Those two rooms had the new materials too, and one of them had a smaller roster, so it suggested the materials and class-size piece might be doing real work independent of coaching.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The setting contains a potential incentive for the coordinator to credit personally delivered coaching for success, because she runs the coaching cycle and is making the recommendation.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant takes the opposite of the requisite biased mechanism: she uses uncoached improvement to reduce confidence in a personally favorable causal account and proposes a design to isolate coaching effects.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: I could have just accepted the gain classrooms and focused all my attention on explaining away the flat ones. Or waited entirely until a full audit was done before forming any impression. I went with checking everything at once instead.
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant identifies a possible confirmatory pathway—accepting favorable evidence while scrutinizing unfavorable evidence—but does not enact it.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The described action is balanced verification and explicit consideration of alternatives. Mentioning a biased alternative is not evidence that the participant used that alternative.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant initially sought verification because testing dates differed between schools.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The scheduling difference is a legitimate measurement-validity concern. The participant checks it across all classrooms, including those with favorable results, which is inconsistent with selective evidence scrutiny.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant experienced board-deadline and agenda-time pressure.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Time pressure is an operational constraint, not a bias mechanism. The text does not show that urgency caused distorted belief updating, evidence selection, or attribution.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant used an aggregate trend line rather than six classroom profiles during a fifteen-minute board presentation.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This is an understandable communication tradeoff. The detailed data remained available and were produced in response to a board question, reducing concern that the aggregation was used to suppress contrary evidence.

nonbias_cues.cue: The five responding teachers reported positive PD feedback.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The favorable response pattern may be nonrepresentative, but the participant expressly notes the small, voluntary sample and possible nonresponse distortion. A data limitation is not evidence of cognitive bias when it is recognized and qualified.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant did not immediately follow up with the nonresponding teacher.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The text provides no evidence that the delay was motivated by avoidance of disconfirming information. It may reflect ordinary workload, timing, or process limitations; the participant subsequently flags the limitation rather than concealing it.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant was personally responsible for coaching four classrooms.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Personal involvement creates an incentive relevant to egocentric attribution, but it does not establish the bias. The participant explicitly distributes causal credit and treats uncoached improvement as evidence against crediting coaching alone.

nonbias_cues.cue: The pilot's results were mixed and the aggregate gain was modest.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Mixed or unfavorable outcomes do not demonstrate a cognitive bias. The relevant question is whether the participant's processing of evidence was systematically distorted, which is not supported here.

causal_claims.claim: Different benchmark-administration days might have distorted fluency results.
causal_claims.evidence: The two schools tested on different days because of a scheduling conflict; the coordinator requested a review across all six classrooms.
causal_claims.assessment: Appropriately treated as a potential measurement threat rather than assumed to be a cause. The subsequent review found day-to-day conditions broadly similar.

causal_claims.claim: Unusually high absenteeism probably explained more of one flat classroom's result than benchmark timing did.
causal_claims.evidence: The specialist identified high absenteeism in one flat classroom during the relevant week.
causal_claims.assessment: Plausible but still tentative and classroom-specific. The use of 'probably' appropriately signals limited causal certainty; the interview does not provide enough detail to establish magnitude or rule out other classroom-specific factors.

causal_claims.claim: Coaching, decodable-text materials, and smaller class size may each have contributed to improved outcomes.
causal_claims.evidence: The improved classrooms were exposed to multiple interventions and contextual differences at the same time; two uncoached classrooms improved while receiving new materials, with one having a smaller roster.
causal_claims.assessment: Causally cautious and well-calibrated. The participant treats the observed associations as confounded rather than as proof that any one factor caused gains.

causal_claims.claim: Materials and class size may contribute independently of direct coaching.
causal_claims.evidence: Two classrooms improved without the coordinator's direct coaching visits, while both had new materials and one had a smaller roster.
causal_claims.assessment: A reasonable hypothesis, not an established causal conclusion. The remaining materials/class-size confounding prevents identification of either factor's independent effect.

causal_claims.claim: Separately tracking classrooms with and without direct coaching in a subsequent round would improve inference about coaching.
causal_claims.evidence: The coordinator proposes a staged approach with materials and coaching available but separate tracking of direct-coaching exposure.
causal_claims.assessment: Directionally sound design improvement. Its inferential value would depend on how classrooms are assigned, whether class size and baseline performance are balanced or measured, and whether implementation fidelity is captured.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Coaching, new materials, and smaller class sizes are bundled in several improving classrooms.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: Observed improvement cannot identify the independent causal contribution of coaching, materials, or roster size.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Classrooms receiving direct coaching may differ at baseline from those that did not receive it.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: Any coached-versus-uncoached comparison in a subsequent round could remain confounded without assignment, matching, baseline adjustment, or careful implementation criteria.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: One classroom's absenteeism is proposed as an explanation for a flat result.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: The explanation is plausible but may be post hoc unless absenteeism data, baseline performance, instructional exposure, and other concurrent disruptions are examined systematically.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The aggregate trend can mask classroom-level variation.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: A modest aggregate gain is not sufficient to establish that the pilot worked consistently, for whom it worked, or which implementation features mattered.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The benchmark-condition assessment appears retrospective and qualitative in the interview.
correlation_causation_risks.implication: The conclusion that date differences were not significant is useful, but its evidentiary strength depends on the review protocol, condition measures, and timing of the assessment.

causal_audit.explanation: No formal paired counterfactual is embedded in this vocabulary-control interview, and none is required by the hidden specification. The interview nevertheless contains useful informal comparative reasoning: the coordinator recognizes that improved classrooms differed on several simultaneous dimensions and that improvement in uncoached classrooms challenges a coaching-only explanation. The proposed next-round design moves toward a more informative comparison, though it should avoid altering coaching exposure together with class size, materials access, or selection criteria if the aim is to estimate coaching's contribution.

global_revision_constraints: Maintain the vocabulary-control requirement of zero defensible occurrences of Biased Assimilation and Egocentric bias.
Do not convert the participant's explicit methodological caution, balanced data verification, or distributed causal attribution into textbook bias language.
Preserve the four-decision-point sequence: uniform data-quality review, constrained board presentation, qualified survey interpretation, and staged causal recommendation.
Retain the distinction between evidence limitations and participant-level cognitive bias.
If any future stylistic revision is made, retain the uncoached improving classrooms and the all-six-classroom testing review because they are key negative evidence against the target biases.
